sections: Design Pillars: What is Central to the Experience?

candidate.description: Drove trucks for years, now runs a dirt track in Hoon. Spends his spare time scaring punks who won't pick up their cigarette butts. Cut-off jean shorts. Zero patience.

llm_verdict.summary: The text is accurate to the docs and has the right tone. The tagline is 35 characters and the description about 167, so both are within limits. The description has four sentences or fragments, and the generator's task required two or three, so it is rejected.

issues.quote: Drove trucks for years, now runs a dirt track in Hoon. Spends his spare time scaring punks who won't pick up their cigarette butts. Cut-off jean shorts. Zero patience.
issues.explanation: The task required a description of two or three short sentences. This has four, and the last two are fragments. The fragments also read as a list of look and personality tags, not a coherent description.
issues.recommendation: Cut it to three sentences or fewer. For example, merge the look detail into one sentence, or drop "Zero patience." and fold "cut-off jean shorts" into the punks sentence. Keep the trucking and dirt-track reflection and stay at 80-220 characters.

issues.explanation: The GDD calls Barry a retired long-haul trucker with years driving cross-country. "Drove trucks" loses the long-haul angle the task asked to reflect.
issues.recommendation: Use "long-haul" or "cross-country" so the trucking past matches the GDD.

candidate.description: Years of long-haul trucking left Barry with a dirt track in Hoon and a bad attitude. He spends his free time beating up punks who won't pick up their cigarette butts.

llm_verdict.summary: No blocking issues. The id and display_name are correct. The tagline is about 35 characters, under the 40 limit. The description is about 165 characters in two sentences, inside the 80-220 range. It reflects Barry's long-haul trucking past and his dirt track in Hoon. The cigarette-butt detail and stubborn attitude come straight from the GDD profile. It adds no invented biography, moves, or match mechanics. The tone is irreverent and suits the game.

issues.quote: Years of long-haul trucking left Barry with a dirt track in Hoon
issues.explanation: This implies trucking is how Barry got the track. The GDD says only that he is a retired trucker who owns the track, so the causal link is a slight embellishment.
issues.recommendation: Optionally decouple them, e.g. "Retired from long-haul trucking, Barry now runs a dirt racing track in Hoon." This is not required.

final.description: Years of long-haul trucking left Barry with a dirt track in Hoon and a bad attitude. He spends his free time beating up punks who won't pick up their cigarette butts.

candidate.description: Expelled at sixteen, Peaux found his calling in backyard wrestling. Years of getting pounded by his football-playing brothers taught him to take a hit. He'd rather wear eyeliner than eye black, and the rednecks can deal with it.

llm_verdict.summary: The text is accurate to the docs, but the description is about 228 characters, over the 220-character limit. That is a blocking limit violation. The facts, id, display_name and tagline are fine.

issues.quote: Expelled at sixteen, Peaux found his calling in backyard wrestling. Years of getting pounded by his football-playing brothers taught him to take a hit. He'd rather wear eyeliner than eye black, and the rednecks can deal with it.
issues.explanation: the description is 228 characters; the UI limit is 80-220.

issues.quote: Expelled at sixteen, Peaux found his calling in backyard wrestling. Years of getting pounded by his football-playing brothers taught him to take a hit. He'd rather wear eyeliner than eye black, and the rednecks can deal with it.
issues.explanation: Description is 228 characters; the style reference is 166. They should be within 35% of each other.

issues.quote: Expelled at sixteen, Peaux found his calling in backyard wrestling. Years of getting pounded by his football-playing brothers taught him to take a hit. He'd rather wear eyeliner than eye black, and the rednecks can deal with it.
issues.explanation: The description is about 228 characters (67 + 83 + 76 plus two spaces). The task caps it at 220, so it violates the stated limit.
issues.recommendation: Cut at least 10 characters. For example, drop 'getting pounded by' and write 'Years of football-playing brothers taught him to take a hit.' Or shorten the last sentence to 'He prefers eyeliner to eye black, and rednecks can deal.' Then recount to confirm it is 220 or fewer.

issues.quote: and the rednecks can deal with it.
issues.explanation: The line is a bit soft for the dark, irreverent Squidbillies and Trailer Park Boys tone. It reads as a generic defiant-outsider line.
issues.recommendation: Add a sharper Southern edge, such as a Duckville reference or a meaner punchline, while staying within the length limit.

candidate.description: Expelled at sixteen, Peaux turned to backyard wrestling. His football-playing brothers made him hard to hurt. He picks eyeliner over eye black, and Duckville's rednecks can choke on it.

llm_verdict.summary: No blocking issues. The id and display_name are correct. The tagline is 28 characters, under the 40 limit. The description is about 185 characters in three short sentences, within 80-220. The facts match the GDD: expelled at sixteen, backyard wrestling, football-playing brothers, eyeliner over eye black, and the neighborhood rednecks. It invents no biography, titles, or moves, and it mentions no match type. The tone is irreverent enough. Two minor polish notes follow.

issues.explanation: This is a fairly generic warning line. It lacks the dark, irreverent trailer-park bite the GDD Tone & Aesthetics section describes.
issues.recommendation: Optional: use a sharper, more Southern-goth line that is still under 40 characters.

issues.quote: His football-playing brothers made him hard to hurt.
issues.explanation: The GDD says his older brothers played college football, and that roughhousing with them gave him a high tolerance for punishment. The text drops 'older' and 'roughhousing', and 'trailer-park goth' is never stated outright. This is not wrong, only less specific.
issues.recommendation: Optionally mention roughhousing with his older brothers, or name the trailer park or goth identity directly.

final.description: Expelled at sixteen, Peaux turned to backyard wrestling. His football-playing brothers made him hard to hurt. He picks eyeliner over eye black, and Duckville's rednecks can choke on it.

messages.text: Pick up your cigarette butts next time, Peaux.
Hot Potato's too hot to handle, and too stubborn to stay down.
Stay down, Peaux. I got a dirt track to run in the morning.
That's what you get for trashin' my driveway, punk.
My brothers hit harder than you, Barry. And they played football.
Nice mustache, Barry. Shame about the nap on the gravel.
Expelled at sixteen. Still smarter than you.

llm_verdict.summary: No blocking issues. All 8 lines use valid ids (4 each, within the 2-4 range) and stay under 90 characters. Spelling of "Peaux" and "Barry" is correct. The lines draw on the docs: Barry's cigarette-butt grudge, dirt track, trailer/driveway and mustache, and Peaux's football brothers, eyeliner and expulsion at sixteen. Every line fits a knockout win. None mentions pinfall, titles or invented moves. The tone is dark and irreverent Southern trailer-park humor. The only issue is a minor one about one weaker line.

issues.quote: Hot Potato's too hot to handle, and too stubborn to stay down.
issues.explanation: It leans on a stock 'too hot to handle' cliché and could fit any wrestling game. It is less specific to the trailer-park setting than Barry's other lines. 'Stubborn to stay down' also reads oddly for a winner.
issues.recommendation: Optionally replace it with a line that uses Barry's trucker or dirt-racer background or his temper, so it sounds more like him.
